Chapter 31: Native Multi-Dimensional Tensors & SIMD Matrix Math

In Python, developers rely on heavy third-party C/C++ extensions like NumPy, PyTorch, or TensorFlow to perform matrix math. In C or Go, developers must write awkward multi-dimensional loops or integrate third-party BLAS/LAPACK libraries.

Cluster-lang provides Native Tensors and SIMD Matrix Mathematics built directly into the language and runtime with zero external dependencies.

This chapter covers:

1. The Native tensor Type and contiguous cache layout.

2. Matrix Multiplication Operators (@ and @=).

3. Auto-Vectorized Cache-Optimized SIMD GEMM (AVX2 / AVX-512).

4. Elementwise Tensor Operations (+, -, ) and Scalar Scaling.

5. Ergonomic Built-in Methods (.rows(), .cols(), .size(), .get(), .set(), .transpose(), .sum(), .dot()).

6. Direct Display via put.

7. The Standard Library Module (std::tensor).

1. Creating Tensors

Tensors can be constructed using native built-ins:

fn main():
    # Create a 2x3 matrix filled with zeros
    z := tensor_zeros(2, 3)

    # Create a 3x3 matrix filled with ones
    o := tensor_ones(3, 3)

    # Create a 2x2 matrix filled with a specific scalar
    f := tensor_fill(2, 2, 42.5)

    # Inspect dimensions
    put "Rows: " + to_text(z.rows())     # 2
    put "Cols: " + to_text(z.cols())     # 3
    put "Size: " + to_text(z.size())     # 6

2. Matrix Multiplication Operator (@ and @=)

Cluster-lang adopts the universal @ operator for matrix multiplication:

fn main():
    # 2x3 Matrix A
    a := tensor_zeros(2, 3)
    a.set(0, 0, 1.0)
    a.set(0, 1, 2.0)
    a.set(0, 2, 3.0)
    a.set(1, 0, 4.0)
    a.set(1, 1, 5.0)
    a.set(1, 2, 6.0)

    # 3x2 Matrix B
    b := tensor_ones(3, 2)

    # Matrix multiplication: (2x3) @ (3x2) -> (2x2)
    c := a @ b
    
    put "Result of A @ B:"
    put c

    # In-place matrix multiply operator:
    multiplier := tensor_fill(2, 2, 2.0)
    c @= multiplier
    put "After c @= multiplier:"
    put c

3. High-Performance Cache-Optimized GEMM

In traditional matrix multiplication, standard i-j-k nested loops jump across memory rows, causing severe cache line evictions.

Cluster-lang's matrix multiplication engine implements a cache-optimized i-k-j traversal loop:

  • Contiguous inner-loop memory strides maximize L1/L2 CPU cache residency.
  • The Clang/LLVM backend automatically auto-vectorizes the inner loops into 256-bit AVX2 / 512-bit AVX-512 SIMD vector instructions.
  • Enjoys near-native BLAS performance without requiring external OpenBLAS or MKL packages.

4. Elementwise Math & Scalar Scaling

You can add, subtract, and multiply tensors elementwise with standard arithmetic operators:

fn main():
    a := tensor_fill(2, 2, 10.0)
    b := tensor_fill(2, 2, 3.0)

    # Elementwise addition (10 + 3 = 13)
    sum := a + b

    # Elementwise subtraction (10 - 3 = 7)
    diff := a - b

    # Elementwise Hadamard multiplication (10 * 3 = 30)
    prod := a * b

    # Scalar scaling (10 * 0.5 = 5)
    scaled := a * 0.5

5. Tensor Inspection & Reductions

Tensors provide rich built-in inspection and reduction methods:

fn main():
    m := tensor_zeros(2, 3)
    # Fill elements...
    
    # Sum all elements in the tensor
    total := m.sum()

    # Transpose the matrix (swap rows and columns)
    mT := m.transpose()
    
    # Vector dot product
    v1 := tensor_fill(1, 4, 2.0)
    v2 := tensor_fill(1, 4, 3.0)
    dot_product := v1.dot(v2)

6. The Standard Library Module (std::tensor)

The standard library includes high-level linear algebra helpers in std/tensor.zk (std/tensor.cl):

import std::tensor

fn main():
    # Identity matrix of size 4x4
    I := eye(4)

    # Convert native vector to tensor
    weights_vec: vector[float] = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]
    W := from_vector(2, 2, weights_vec)

    # Convert tensor back to vector
    out_vec := to_vector(W)
